curriculum.title: Radical Reformation and Believers' Church Traditions

core.big_idea: Radical reform movements emphasised believer's baptism, discipleship, and church-state separation under severe pressure.

passages.reading_note: Read in immediate context; select age-appropriate portions without changing the claim.

core.metanarrative_position: Jesus' ministry: Reformation within the History, Hope, and Independent Faith cycle

claims.statement: The selected passage supplies the main textual evidence central to Radical Reformation and Believers' Church Traditions.
Radical reform movements emphasised believer's baptism, discipleship, and church-state separation under severe pressure.

Believer’s baptism is the curriculum’s framework position, while Radical Reformation history is used to study how some Christians recovered or defended that conviction under particular historical conditions.
claims.interpretive_hinge: The baptism conclusion is argued from New Testament conversion texts; historical Anabaptist evidence shows later belief and practice but does not independently prove the doctrine.
claims.prohibited_overstatement: Do not present this framework conclusion as an explicit biblical command or quotation.

core.interpretation_skill: Evaluate sources and arguments; identify assumptions; compare credible positions; state uncertainty precisely

learning.foundation_objective: Analyse the relevant text and explain the case that radical reform movements emphasised believer's baptism, discipleship, and church-state separation under severe pressure.
learning.extension_objective: Test the claim against context, genre, canonical synthesis, credible alternatives, and the limits of the available evidence.
know: The principal passage is Matthew 28:18-20; selected Anabaptist texts.

practise: Retell or analyse the passage using evidence from the text.

become: A learner who responds to Scripture with trust, wisdom, worship, service, repentance, love, courage, or humility as appropriate.
success_evidence: Student can summarize the selected passage.

theological_guardrails: Publication requires verified Anabaptist/Radical Reformation sources and careful distinction among movements that were not institutionally identical.

Church-state separation claims should be historically sourced and not projected uniformly onto every Radical Reformation group.
